body.text: in brief
• Ukranian leaders and political opponents had condemned the idea of Albanese taking a photo alongside Putin.
• Trump will meet with Putin and Xi on the sidelines of APEC for a historic trilateral later on Thursday.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has appeared in a photo alongside Russian President Vladimir Putin on the opening night of APEC in China, despite calls from some Ukrainian groups and political opponents to avoid the group shot.
After arriving on Wednesday afternoon, the prime minister was photographed with about 20 other regional leaders at an opening-night banquet next to Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney.
Both leaders had said they wanted to avoid offending their Chinese hosts by removing themselves from the picture, describing it as a mark of "respect".
"I will bear in mind the wishes of our host," Albanese told reporters in Shenzhen after being asked if he'd appear in an "APEC family photo" alongside Putin.
"If you are invited to an event … I respect that, but we'll also make our position very clear when it comes to Ukraine."
Another official photo is scheduled for Thursday morning.

United States President Donald Trump and his Russian counterpart are both in attendance, representing their countries as members of the economic forum and for a historic trilateral with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Upon landing, Albanese reiterated Australia's opposition to the war in Ukraine, which began after Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. Russia's war must end on "Ukraine's terms", and all global conflicts must be de-escalated, Albanese said.
On Monday, the Australian Federation of Ukrainian Organisations said being in a photo alongside Putin would ignore Russia's "gross violations of international norms".

"Vladimir Putin is not just another world leader attending an international summit. He is an indicted war criminal and the architect of a brutal war against Ukraine — a war that has brought death, destruction and unimaginable suffering to millions of people," federation chair Kateryna Argyrou said.
Ukrainian ambassador Vasyl Myroshnychenko told SBS News earlier this week he'd hoped Albanese would "continue to be guided by Australia's very prominent pro-Ukraine stance" when it came to the photo.
"Substance matters more to Ukraine than style."
Greens leader David Shoebridge and Liberal senator Andrew Bragg have both criticised the group photo.
Foreign Minister Penny Wong avoided a similar photo with Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov at the G20 meeting in the US last month.
The 21-nation international gathering will run until Thursday evening, following the main closed-door discussions. Regional trade, security, and the energy transition are all on the agenda.
Albanese met with Trump after his arrival on Wednesday. Both had participated in talks in the Philippines on Tuesday with the leaders of India and Japan.
The prime minister is expected to meet with Xi on Friday morning and participate in bilateral talks with the heads of Mexico, Canada, Singapore, and New Zealand.
Historic trilateral looms large

For the first time, the leaders of Russia, China and the US will sit at the same table for a joint political gathering on Thursday. US officials have confirmed the three-way meeting on the sidelines of the APEC conference.
Trump will also meet with Putin individually, officials have confirmed, while a dialogue with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un is still hoped for.

The Russian leader has not appeared at an APEC summit since 2017, as previous hosts are members of the International Criminal Court, which has a warrant for his arrest. However, China is not a signatory, and his appearance allows him to sidestep European-led efforts to isolate Russia diplomatically.

It is expected that ongoing tariffs and other trade frictions, as well as artificial intelligence safety and information sharing, will be discussed at the trilateral, pushed by Trump, whose Republican Party suffered major losses in the US midterm elections.

The meeting has been likened to the historic Yalta conference between Joseph Stalin, Franklin D Roosevelt and Winston Churchill, the "big three" leaders of the Soviet Union, the US, and the United Kingdom who met in the final year of World War Two to shape the post-war globe.
Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed concern about the meeting, but Albanese has said that "in general" it is a "good thing" for countries to speak to each other.
"At a time when there are more conflicts than at any time since the Second World War … we want to see more dialogue, less military conflict," he said.
Albanese pushes AI safety

While the APEC meeting risks being overshadowed by the tripartite discussion between the world's major powers, Albanese has used the opportunity to promote Australian goods and interests on the world's stage.

In a speech at the summit, the Labor leader spoke of Australia's plan for AI standards, saying the controversial technology could bring new prosperity to the Asia-Pacific region as long as safety, security and social licence were assured.
"The economic potential and opportunity of artificial intelligence is enormous," he said. "Not just for the Asia-Pacific, but for the world."

Following Carney, who also touted AI governance and is famous for his "middle powers" push, Albanese said there was still a role for middle-weight nations like Australia to use their influence on global affairs.
